about: What an employee costs an employer, for tools/build-employer-cost-pages.js: employer (secondary) Class 1 National Insurance, Employment Allowance and automatic enrolment pension minimums, each quoted from GOV.UK. The employer NI rate, threshold and Employment Allowance must match data/uk/rates-2026-27.json (the build checks). Changes each April.

class1a.quote: The National Insurance Class 1A rate on expenses and benefits for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.

allowance.quote: Employment Allowance allows eligible employers to reduce their annual National Insurance liability by up to £10,500.

allowanceNot.quote: You also cannot claim if your company has just one director and that director is the only employee liable for secondary Class 1 National Insurance.

allowancePublic.quote: You cannot claim if you’re a public body or business doing more than half your work in the public sector (such as local councils and NHS services) - unless you’re a charity.

pensionBand.quote: In most automatic enrolment schemes, you’ll make contributions based on your total earnings between £6,240 and £50,270 a year before tax.

pensionMin.quote: The minimum your employer pays You pay Total minimum contribution From April 2019 3% 5% 8%

levy.quote: Apprenticeship Levy is an amount paid at a rate of 0.5% of an employer’s annual pay bill. As an employer, you have to pay Apprenticeship Levy each month if you: have an annual pay bill of more than £3 million

levyAllowance.quote: The allowance reduces the amount of Apprenticeship Levy you have to pay by £15,000 across the year.
